title: A commit from a checkout behind its moved branch is refused
why: Lane notes-fix-guard-2: three resumed agents kept a stale index or tree after their branch moved (coordinator, 17:07 CST Nov 7). The harm is a silent undo of pushed work.
note: Related steps: one-worktree-per-branch, checkout-b-current-branch. Done check: a red test where a commit from a checkout behind its moved branch is refused, and a fast-forward pull still passes. Absorbs proposed steps one-branch-one-worktree (lane past-ruling-on-send) and one-branch-per-writer (lane reviewer-no-session-tools), coordinator 18:19 CST Nov 7. Incident: a lane ran three writer agents in parallel on one branch, each in its own worktree; two hit stale indexes after the branch moved, and those indexes staged a reversal of hooks/guard.py (both caught before commit). Add a red test where a commit whose index differs from HEAD's tree beyond the staged paths is refused or warned. Lane, 18:20 CST: the added case is covered by decision stale-tree-commit (on branch lane/resumed-agent-stale-tree). A commit is refused, not warned, when a staged path holds the copy from the pre-move commit (read from the HEAD reflog) that the move changed. Fourth incident, folded by the coordinator at 19:14 CST Nov 7 (proposed step brief-branch-held): lane report-model-from-role briefed two agents onto one branch, lane/rmfr-build, at 18:40 CST, and one worktree got foreign staging. Add a refusal for a brief whose checkout -B names a branch another live worktree holds. Fifth incident (lane mutate-sweep-control, via the coordinator 19:43 CST Nov 7): a builder ran checkout -B on a branch the lane's own worktree held, and the ref moved under the lane. Sixth incident (lane qmax-ste-lint-in-narrow-checks, via the coordinator 19:48 CST): a builder that commits on the lane branch from its own worktree leaves the parent checkout with a stale copy that looks like uncommitted work. Seventh and eighth incidents (via the coordinator 19:54 CST): lane check-tail-wrapper-forms twice had two worktrees share one local branch ref, leaving stale staged files, once for its builder and once for the lane; it worked around this with a detached worktree. Ninth to eleventh incidents (via the coordinator 20:14 CST; decision stale-tree-commit in round 3): a test-author moved its worktree to a newer head and left stale staged files that would revert the builder's work; each time a commit with --only or a read-tree repair saved it. Guard idea: refuse an agent's commit when the index differs from HEAD in files the agent never wrote. If round 3 does not cover that form, it becomes this step's follow-up, owner coordinator. Built as #1740 (rule stale-tree-commit), round 3 PASS, with runner 8 (coordinator 20:28 CST). Lane answer, 20:29 CST: round 3 covers the ninth-to-eleventh form by the move itself; the guard reads the old head from the worktree's HEAD log and refuses a commit that stages the old copy of a file the move changed. Known limit, note stale-tree-two-entry-window: only the newest two HEAD-log entries are read, so two intervening commits clear it. No follow-up step unless that limit bites. Twelfth incident (lane qmax-narration-in-narrow-checks, q_max, 21:10 CST, via the coordinator 21:11): a resumed builder's index showed test files deleted after other agents pushed; a read-tree repair saved it, nothing lost. The coordinator asked the #1740 lane whether its rule covers a ref moved by another worktree or by a fetch. Added 21:12 CST. Related incident from lane auto-merge-refused (#1763): an agent moved a held branch (agent-moves-held-branch; coordinator, 21:41 CST Nov 7). Incident, Nov 7 23:39 CST (lane revive-1042, #1042): another worktree's checkout moved a worktree's branch, which left a lane's tree stale. Coordinator: a held step for a guard; folded here, since this step refuses a commit from a checkout behind its moved branch. Related sighting (lane notes-fix-large-3, 07:18 CST Nov 8; proposed step scratch-detached-merges, folded here): an agent's push to the branch a scratch worktree had checked out left that worktree with a stale index. The lane's fix: a scratch worktree works detached. Sighting (lane runner-drops-handed-lane, session_013NEJKyzg9A9SDZ926jRCSU, 15:53 CST Nov 8; it proposed step shared-ref-stale-index, folded here): a builder in its own worktree moved local ref lane/runner-drops-handed-lane to d8a855e55 while the orchestrator's worktree had that branch checked out; the orchestrator's index went stale and git showed the reverse of the new commits as staged. The commit-and-push Stop hook then asked to commit them, which would have pushed a revert of the fix. Caught by a diff against the old commit. Guard ideas: this step's refusal of a commit from a checkout behind its moved branch, or the Stop hook checks HEAD's tree is not behind the branch tip. The ref move itself is step push-branch-held-elsewhere's.
